samples.title: Sorting press: Proof strip
samples.statement:
Two small sorted proof trays are repeatedly joined by the office's divide-and-merge press. Rafi rolls a fresh proof strip into the office typewriter. The supervisor wants the readings in their precise working order before signing the file.

Produce readings sorted numerically ascending using a merge-based divide-and-conquer approach. Keep duplicate readings.

Return the entire derived sequence, preserving its order.

Implement sortingPressProofStrip(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

samples.title: Sorting press: Peak ticket
samples.statement:
Two small sorted proof trays are repeatedly joined by the office's divide-and-merge press. Ada is setting the upper stop on an old office gauge. The largest derived reading goes on its label, even if the whole tray is below zero.

Produce readings sorted numerically ascending using a merge-based divide-and-conquer approach. Keep duplicate readings.

Return the largest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. Negative maxima must remain negative.

Implement sortingPressPeakTicket(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.

samples.title: Sorting press: Boss receipt
samples.statement:
Two small sorted proof trays are repeatedly joined by the office's divide-and-merge press. Neri adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

Produce readings sorted numerically ascending using a merge-based divide-and-conquer approach. Keep duplicate readings.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement sortingPressBossReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
